To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EL spectra of irradiated and forward biased GaP:Zin,O LEDs reveal a growth of sharp, Zn-related bound exciton emission lines in the 580 nm to -620 nm range.
gamma irradiation and/or forward bias can cause the appearance of sharp, bound-exciton emission lines in the EL spectrum of GaP LEDs at low temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the low temperature (76 K) electroluminescent (EL) spectra from gallium phosphide (GaP) light emitting diodes.
the effects of high current forward bias on the electroluminescent spectra of GaP light emitting diodes.
the effects of gamma radiation and forward bias on GaP:Zin,O LEDs and their 76 K EL emission spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gamma irradiation of GaP: Zn,O LEDs produces a defect which is not present in non-irradiated LEDs, but which can be created in non-irradidated LEDs by high current forward bias.
the Z lines are due to the recombination of excitons bound to the zinc interstitial.
gamma irradiation of GaP: Zn,O LEDs enhances the effects of high current forward bias on the electroluminescent spectra.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Z lines are not due to a defect introduced by irradiation but rather to a defect already present in some LEDs, which is made mobile and/or more active by recombination-enhanced diffusion.
gamma radiation and high-current bias can cause the formation of the Z lines and, in some cases, the growth of the Z1 line to a level where it dominates the EL spectrum.

the 76 K EL spectrum of the Zn,O LED is a complex superposition of several types of recombination processes, and that the effects of irradiation and forward current on the spectrum are complex and not fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 580 nm to the 620 nm Z line emission in GaP:ZnP is a signature of the recombination-enhancement motion of a Zn interstitial.
the EL spectra are a sensitive tool for detecting defects which are present at very low levels and are otherwise difficult to detect by other means.
